detect.visual_cues: Blue Alipay app chrome. Screens with a bank-card form (card number, expiry, CVV), a red or grey failure banner, a passport-upload prompt, a QR payment code page, or a mini-program named TourCard.

entries.title: Set up Alipay before you fly
entries.why: Most shops, taxis and metro gates in China take mobile payment only. Setting up at home on Wi-Fi takes 10 minutes and avoids doing it jet-lagged with no data.
steps: Install Alipay from the App Store or Google Play. Outside China it opens in English automatically.
Sign up with your own mobile number (any country) and enter the SMS code. No Chinese number or Chinese bank account is needed.
Tap Me > Bank Cards > Add Now. Set a 6-digit payment password, then add one mainstream credit card: Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Discover, Diners Club or UnionPay.
Tap Me > Settings > Account & Security > Identity Verification. Upload your passport photo page and do the face check. Do this now, not later.
entries.fallback: If the card will not link, see Card won't link. If you prefer not to link a card, open TourCard inside Alipay as a prepaid wallet.

entries.title: Card won't link to Alipay
entries.why: Alipay asks your bank to approve the card. Banks often block an unfamiliar Chinese merchant, and debit, prepaid and virtual cards fail more than mainstream credit cards.
steps: Try a different card first: a credit card from a major bank on another network (Visa if Mastercard failed, or the reverse). Fintech cards such as Wise or Revolut succeed more often than traditional bank cards.

In your banking app turn on International transactions and Online purchases, wait 10 minutes, then add the card again. If it still fails, call the bank: say you are in China paying through Alipay and the merchant will show as Alipay or Ant Group.

Make the name on the card, your passport and your Alipay profile match exactly, including middle names, then finish Identity Verification (Me > Settings > Account & Security) before adding the card again.
Still refused: set up Nihao China instead. It is the official inbound-visitor app, registers with email or Apple ID, links Visa, Mastercard and UnionPay, and does not depend on an Alipay card link.
entries.fallback: Open TourCard inside Alipay as a prepaid wallet, or withdraw cash at a Bank of China ATM with your foreign card. Alipay English support: +86 571 2688 6000, daily 08:00-24:00.

entries.title: No SMS code from Alipay
entries.why: The code goes to the number you registered with. After landing, many phones are on a new eSIM or have roaming off, so the SMS to your home number never arrives.
steps: Make sure the SIM that owns your registered number can receive texts: turn on roaming for that line, or switch it back on if you disabled it for an eSIM.
On the code screen choose the voice-call option if offered. Alipay can read the code out in an automated call.
Wait 60 seconds before requesting again. Repeated taps can lock requests for a few minutes.
Check your country code is correct on the login screen and that the number has no leading zero.
entries.fallback: If your home number cannot receive texts in China at all, you cannot log in until it can: turn roaming on for that line, or contact Alipay support at +86 571 2688 6000 to change the registered number.

entries.title: Payment failed at the counter
entries.why: Three different things look the same at the counter: your bank refused the charge, the shop showed a personal collection code that foreign cards cannot pay, or you hit a limit. Alipay prints a short reason on the failure screen.
steps: Ask the cashier to scan YOUR code instead: open Pay/Receive and show the barcode. Foreign cards cannot pay a person's own collection QR, only registered merchant codes, and scanning their code at a stall or small shop fails for that reason.
Issuer declined or Bank declined means your bank. Retry once, then turn on international and online payments in your banking app, or call the bank to allow charges from Alipay / Ant Group in China.

Limit exceeded or a request for ID means you hit the unverified allowance. Complete Identity Verification (Me > Settings > Account & Security), then pay again. For large amounts, ask to split the bill.
Quick test: try the same card for a small payment in WeChat Pay. If both fail, it is the card or bank. If only Alipay fails, reopen Alipay, update it, and switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data.
entries.fallback: Pay with cash. Every merchant in China must accept RMB cash by law; withdraw at a Bank of China ATM with your foreign card. If the account says it is locked, see Account locked.

entries.title: Alipay asks for your passport
entries.why: Chinese rules let you spend a small total without ID. Past that, or for larger single payments, Alipay must verify your passport before it lets the payment through.
steps: Tap Me > Settings > Account & Security > Identity Verification. When asked for region choose Non-Mainland China, then Passport. Choosing Mainland China asks for a Chinese ID number and fails.

Photograph the passport photo page flat, in daylight, no glare, all four corners visible. If offered, scan the passport's NFC chip instead by holding the phone on the back cover; it skips the photo check and succeeds more often.
Type your name exactly as the passport prints it, including middle names and suffixes, and make the linked card's name match. For the face check, face a window, remove glasses, hold still.
Wait. Most checks finish within minutes; manual reviews take up to 24 hours. After 3 to 5 failed attempts the flow locks for 24 hours, so stop retrying and wait.
entries.fallback: Still rejected after a day: contact Alipay support in the app (Me > Settings > Help Center) or call +86 571 2688 6000 for a manual review, which takes 1 to 3 working days. Meanwhile use Nihao China or cash.

entries.title: Use TourCard when your card won't link
entries.why: TourCard is a prepaid wallet inside Alipay issued by a Chinese bank. You top it up from your foreign card, so it works even when direct card linking is refused. It costs more per top-up.
steps: In Alipay, type TourCard in the top search bar and open the mini-program.
Register with your passport when prompted.
Top up from a Visa, Mastercard, JCB or Diners Club card. A service charge is added to each top-up; the exact rate is shown before you confirm.
Pay as usual with Pay/Receive or Scan. TourCard is for paying merchants only, not for sending money to people.
entries.fallback: If TourCard also refuses your card, use cash from a Bank of China ATM, or check whether your home e-wallet is part of the Alipay+ network and can scan Chinese codes directly.

entries.title: How to pay at a shop with Alipay
entries.why: There are two directions: the cashier scans you, or you scan the shop's printed code. Small stalls usually have a printed code; chains and taxis scan you.
steps: To be scanned: open Alipay, tap Pay/Receive at the top, hold the barcode and QR code to the scanner. Enter your 6-digit payment password if asked.
To scan them: tap Scan, point at the shop's printed QR code, type the amount the cashier tells you, confirm.
Check the confirmation screen for the amount and any fee line, then confirm.
Online, choose Alipay at checkout; the site opens the app or shows a QR code for you to scan.
entries.fallback: If the code will not scan, ask the cashier to scan yours instead, or pay cash.

entries.title: Call a DiDi ride from inside Alipay
entries.why: DiDi inside Alipay needs no Chinese phone number and charges your linked card automatically. The WeChat version of DiDi may refuse accounts without a Chinese number.
steps: Open Alipay and type DiDi in the top search bar, or tap the DiDi icon on the home screen.
Allow location, confirm the pickup pin, type the destination in English or Chinese.
Pick a ride type (Express is the cheapest), confirm. The fare is charged to your linked card after the ride.
When the car arrives, match the licence plate with the one shown. The driver may ask for the last 4 digits of your phone number; show them on screen.
entries.fallback: Use the in-app chat; messages are translated automatically. For help, DiDi has 24/7 English support under Account > Help.

entries.title: Alipay says your account is locked or restricted
entries.why: Too many failed card links, verification attempts or payments in a short time trigger a temporary risk lock. It usually lifts by itself; retrying makes it longer.
steps: Stop retrying. Note the exact message and the time.
Make sure you are on a normal mobile or Wi-Fi connection without any network tool that routes traffic abroad; Alipay's risk system flags foreign-looking traffic.
Wait 24 hours, then open Alipay once and check whether the lock has lifted.
If it has not, contact support in the app (Me > Settings > Help Center > Contact Us) with your passport number, registered phone and a screenshot of the message.
entries.fallback: Use Nihao China or cash in the meantime. Alipay English support: +86 571 2688 6000, daily 08:00-24:00.

entries.title: Use Nihao China when Alipay won't take your card
entries.why: Nihao China is the official app for inbound visitors, run by China UnionPay. It registers with email or Apple ID, needs no Chinese phone number, links Visa, Mastercard and UnionPay, and charges no platform fee on QR payments.
steps: Install Nihao China from the App Store or Google Play. Register with email, Apple ID or Google if SMS codes are not reaching you.
Complete identity verification with your passport when prompted.
Tap Profile > Tour Wallet > Bank Card > +. Enter the card details and pass your bank's one-time check; a 1 yuan pre-authorisation is taken and refunded.
Pay with Pay (show your code) or Scan (scan the shop's code), the same two ways as Alipay.
entries.fallback: If Nihao China also refuses the card, top up its Tour Wallet from the card instead (small load fee), or use cash.
